In the summer of 1964 Manzione was assigned to SOG's northern headquarters in Dong Ha. "Back then," he said, "being as close to the DMZ as we were, it was hard to tell where any particular Vietnamese civilian came from." Here he referred to the fact that the demilitarized zone separated families and communities without regard for their political affiliations. In light of this ambiguity, counterterror was one way of co-opting uncommitted civilians. To facilitate their political awakening, according to Manzione, "We left our calling card nailed to the forehead of the corpses we left behind. They were playing card size with a light green skull with red eyes and red teeth dripping blood, set against a black background. We hammered them into the third eye, the pituitary gland, with our pistol butts. The third eye is the seat of consciousness for Buddhists, and this was a form of mutilation that had a powerful psychological effect."
Curiously, terror tactics often involve mutilating the third eye (the seat of insight and secret thoughts) and playing on fears of an "all-seeing" cosmic eye of God. Used by morale officers in World War I, the eye of God trick called for pilots in small aircraft to fly over enemy camps and call out the names of individual soldiers. Ed Lansdale applied the technique in the Philippines. "At night, when the town was asleep, a psywar team would creep into town and paint an eye (copied from the Egyptian eye that appears atop the pyramid in the Great Seal of the United States) on a wall facing the house of each suspect," Lansdale writes. "The mysterious presence of these malevolent eyes the next morning had a sharply sobering effect." [6]
To appreciate the "sobering effects" of the "malevolent" and "mysterious" eye of God, it helps to know something of the archetype's mythological origins. In ancient Egypt, the eye of God was plucked from Horus, an anthropomorphic sun-god with a falcon's head. Pictured as the morning sun cresting a pyramid, the eye of God represents the dawn of self-awareness, when the ego emerged from the id and no longer required human sacrifice to overcome its primeval anxiety. Awed by the falcon's superlative sight, talons, and flight, the Egyptians endowed Horus with the bird's predatory prowess, so he could avenge the murder his father, Osiris, whose name means "seat of the eye." Set on high, scanning the earth for the forces of darkness, the falcon as sun-god -- as the manifestation of enlightenment -- carries out the work of organization and pacification, imposing moral order on earth.
The eye of God assumes its mysterious "counterespionage" qualities through this myth of the eternal cycle -- the battle between good and evil -- in which, if the perfidious gods of darkness can guess the sun-god's secret name, they can rob him of his powers and trap him forever in the underworld. Thus a falcon emblem was placed above the gates of all Egyptian temples, scanning for the sun-god's enemies, while the sun-god relied on code names to conceal his identity.
Oddly enough, the eye of God was the symbol of the Cao Dai sect, whose gallery of saints include Confucius, Buddha, Joan of Arc, Jesus, and Victor Hugo. Inside the Cao Dai cathedral in Tay Ninh City, the Cao Dai pope divined upon his planchette the secrets of the Great pyramid; over the temple door loomed a huge blue "all-seeing" eye surrounded by snakes and trees. For this reason, some people suggest that the Cao Dai eye of God endowed Phoenix, the all-seeing bird of prey that selectively snatched its prey, with its ubiquity.
In South Vietnam the eye of God trick took a ghastly twist. CIA officer Pat McGarvey recalled to Seymour Hersh that "some psychological warfare guy in Washington thought of a way to scare the hell out of villagers. When we killed a VC there, they wanted us to spread-eagle the guy, put out his eye, cut a hole in the back [of his head] and put his eye in there. The idea was that fear was a good weapon." Likewise, ears were cut off corpses and nailed to houses to let the people know that Big Brother was listening as well.
33
The subliminal purpose of terror tactics was to drive people into a state of infantile dependence. In this sense, CIA psywar experts were not exorcists come to heal Vietnam and free it from Communist demons; their spells were meant to break up the society and project its repressed homicidal impulses onto the Communists -- cast as carrion and snakes.
"It was all part of the counterterror doctrine developed by the Ugly American to beat the enemy at his own game," Elton Manzione said. In beating the VC at their own game, the SEALs were told to ignore the rules of engagement. "Our camp was always separate," he explained. "Just CTs and us. Sometimes a Special Forces colonel would walk in, but rarely. Nam Dong was not populated by the spooky hunter-killer type folks you associate with the Green Berets. A lot of them were medical specialists, or agricultural specialists, or language specialists that worked with the villagers on different things. So the great majority of this particular Special Forces camp were not hit team types. We were, however, and our camp was separated by wire and a gate.
"Now everyone knows about the airborne interrogation -- taking three people up in a chopper, taking one guy and saying, 'Talk,' then throwing him out before he even gets the chance to open his mouth. Well, we wrapped det [detonator] cord around their necks and wired them to the detonator box. And basically what it did was blow their heads off. The interrogator would tell the translator, usually a South Vietnamese intelligence officer, 'Ask him this.' He'd ask him, 'Who gave you the gun?' And the guy would start to answer, or maybe he wouldn't -- maybe he'd resist -- but the general idea was to waste the first two. They planned the snatches that way. Pick up this guy because we're pretty sure he's VC cadre -- these other two guys just run errands for him. Or maybe they're nobody; Tran, the farmer, and his brother Nguyen. But bring in two. Put them in a row. By the time you get to your man, he's talking so fast you got to pop the weasel just to shut him up." After a moment's silence he added, "I guess you could say that we wrote the book on terror."
Having seen the intelligence potential in Scotton's PATs and CTs, DeSilva, according to Stu Methven, "decided he wanted a version in each province in South Vietnam." The job of standardizing the political action teams, along with the counterterrorists and Chau's Census Grievance program, was given to Methven, whose first step was to find them a permanent home on the Vung Tau Peninsula. Methven did this with the help of Tran Quoc Buu, a wealthy Vietnamese warlord and founding member of the Can Lao party who in 1954 had headed the CIA-funded Vietnamese Federation of Labor. Buu had been charged by Diem with laundering Can Lao rake offs through the federation's foreign accounts. Buu, however, pocketed the money and used it to buy huge parcels of land, including a portion of Vung Tau.
After the coup the tables turned on Buu, whose association with Diem led to his imprisonment; in need of cash to buy his way out of jail, he sold Methven a choice piece of property on the Vung Tau Peninsula. Located at Cat Lo, Buu's estate had been used by the French as a transshipment point in their lucrative opium trade and as a training camp for their Montagnard maquis. Buu himself had used Cat Lo as a training camp for his private army of resettled Catholic refugees. Called the Shrimp and Cinnamon Soldiers, for their civilian jobs, Buu's troops were highly motivated and, according to Methven, were admired by Nguyen Van Thieu because "unlike the ARVN, they stayed at their posts at night." With Thieu's consent, Methven arranged for CIA contract employees to start training counterterror, census grievance, and political action cadres at Buu's Vung Tau facility. This was a unilateral CIA operation, extralegal, with no GVN oversight. Isolated and accessible only by Air America, Vung Tau was the perfect place for such a covert action undertaking.
Vung Tau became the seedbed of the CIA's political cadres, who were trained to enter VC villages, to convince the people that the GVN represented their interests and, having done that, to help the villagers form self-defense forces to fight the VC. However, the generals who dominated the GVN viewed the image of an armed citizenry with alarm and were reluctant to support the program. Even MACV commander Westmoreland argued that anyone with a gun should be in the army. Thus, before the GVN could join the synthesis, it first had to put its house in order -- which, in the summer of 1964, was a remote possibility at best.
To begin with, the Montagnards had mutinied against their Special Forces officers in Ban Me Thuot and four other districts, temporarily diverting the CIA's attention. Meanwhile, the Dai Viets had assumed control of the government, created a Directorate of Political Warfare, and established their own pacification program managed by Professor Nguyen Van Huy. Called Rural Construction and centered in Thu Duc, the program used mobile cadre teams to organize villagers into pro-GVN associations. But the Dai Viets were split internally over the issue of allowing VNQDD cadres into the program, and when other, more powerful Dai Viets launched an unsuccessful coup against General Khanh in April, Huy and his associates were exiled once again.
With the CIDG program and the GVN in shambles, the CIA looked to its nascent Vung Tau program for stability. The CIA officer chosen to build the facility and create a national pacification program that could maintain operations independently of the GVN by fostering local initiatives was a garrulous, blustering Irish-American named Tom Donohue. A product and practitioner of Cook County politics, Donohue resembled W.C. Fields in looks and mannerisms and, you get the feeling, in ethics, too; to wit, he joined the CIA when he perceived the cold war as "a growth industry." When he spoke, his words came in melodramatic exclamations. As he
34
pondered, he paced nervously, like a pool hustler circling the table, picking his next shot. In all these respects, Donohue was the prototypical CIA officer -- a cagey position player using a glib exterior to mask a calculating mind.
When we met in 1986, Tom Donohue was working as the Mideast representative for a Filipino construction company. When he arrived in Saigon twenty-two years earlier to replace Cliff Strathern as chief of covert action, he worked under State Department cover in the embassy's political office. One of his jobs at the time, he said, was managing "a small training camp down in Vung Tau which had about a hundred students run by a very dynamic guy -- Le Xuan Mai.
"I spent a lot of time with Mai," Donohue recalled, "and was mighty impressed. Mai was a wizard at appealing to a particular sensory element the Vietnamese seemed to have about the fatherland. He had the ability to interweave Vietnamese myth and modern-day nationalism that seemed somehow to make an impact on the tutored and the untutored alike. He was trilingual," Donohue said with admiration, "but he was controversial. What kind of army officer goes around talking about fairies and dragons?" [8]
Donohue immediately picked up where Stu Methven had left off, hammering out a deal with the minister of the interior to rent an even larger chunk of the Vung Tau Peninsula. He then got Mai a promotion to major and arranged for "a guy who had been training agency people to come up with three or four others to run the camp. This is an early program called armed propaganda team," what he termed an armed social working element.
"Anyway," Donohue said, "I decided this was the route we should be following, and I began looking for a means of expanding the program. I got rid of most of the other stuff I had responsibility for, and from that point on programming evolved rapidly. We began to build up the program with more and more officers coming in from Washington on permanent change of station."
Donohue leased a Catholic seminary, whose owners had "decided it was time to cut and run," and used Seminary Camp, as it became known, as headquarters for his staff. "It was really just a stopgap," Donohue explained, "but it gave us the ability to have a good permanent base.

🇺🇸🇨🇦 Stellantis is gone from Brampton. It is never coming back.

The plant has been sold to Roshel. The Jeep Compass that was once planned for the site has already moved to Illinois. More than 2,000 workers have been on indefinite layoff since 2023, and the sale ends vehicle assembly there. Calling everyone back to a bargaining table does not reverse a completed commercial decision driven by tariffs, market size, and capital allocation.

Canada sells 90-95% of its vehicle production into the U.S. When tariffs stay in place and the larger market offers clearer conditions for new capacity, manufacturers place growth investment south of the border. Honda’s new Ohio plant and Stellantis’ Illinois shift are the pattern. Public statements that “walking away is not an option” do not change the economics or recover the production that has already left. 

If Mélanie Joly truly cared about Unifor autoworkers and their jobs, she would be on a plane to Washington to set up a signing ceremony for the updated USMCA agreement before more industrial plants close up shop and walk away.

text:
It is not a law yet!

**No, it is not already a law.**

The idea of eliminating property taxes for Americans aged 65 and older who own their homes outright is not a federal law, and it is not in effect nationwide. Property taxes are set and collected by state and local governments (to fund schools, police, infrastructure, and other services). The federal government does not levy property taxes and has no direct authority to abolish or uniformly eliminate them.

### What the claim actually is

The X post frames this as a Trump proposal. Fact-checkers, including Snopes (August 2026), rated the claim that Trump proposed eliminating these property taxes as **false**. A White House spokesperson told Snopes that Trump “has not stated this.” No major news outlets reported such a proposal, and searches turned up no supporting evidence. Online claims and some AI-generated videos appear to have mixed it up with other senior tax relief measures.

### What *is* law (related senior tax relief)

In 2025, Congress passed and Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB). It includes a temporary enhanced deduction for seniors:

- Up to $6,000 additional deduction for taxpayers age 65+ (or $12,000 for a married couple if both qualify).
- Available through 2028, with income phase-outs (generally full benefit below ~$75,000 single / $150,000 joint).
- This is a **federal income tax** benefit. It reduces taxable income and, for many Social Security recipients, effectively lowers or eliminates federal income tax on those benefits. It is **not** a property tax exemption.

The law also raised the SALT (state and local tax) deduction cap, which can indirectly help some people who itemize and pay high property taxes, but again this is not an elimination of property taxes.

### State and local level

No state fully eliminates property taxes for all homeowners 65+ who own their homes outright. Nearly every state offers some form of senior relief (exemptions on part of the home’s value, assessment freezes, credits, or deferrals), often with income limits, residency requirements, or application processes. These vary widely by state and even by county. Some states and localities are actively debating broader cuts or phase-outs of homeowner property taxes (for example, discussions involving Florida, Georgia, and others), sometimes with a focus on seniors, but these are not a uniform national policy.

In short: the specific measure described in the post is not law. Seniors may qualify for existing state/local property tax relief programs (check with your county assessor) and for the federal senior income-tax deduction under the 2025 law, but there is no nationwide elimination of property taxes for 65+ outright homeowners.

The White House press secretary position is currently vacant following the departure of Katie Zacharia, who reportedly served only five days in the role.

🌎 WORLD NEWS TODAY
Monday, November 9, 2026
GLOBAL HEADLINES | AMERICA • WAR • ECONOMY • CLIMATE • FAITH • TECHNOLOGY
🇺🇸 1. UNITED STATES — ELECTION UPHEAVAL RESHAPES WASHINGTON
Democrats' sweeping November 3 midterm victories have transformed American politics, putting them on course to control Congress when lawmakers take office January 3, 2027.

President Donald Trump faces growing congressional opposition over the Iran war, immigration enforcement and government spending.
Republican Representative Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging unlawful military actions. Hegseth disputes the criticism, and Trump continues defending him. The allegations have not been adjudicated.

Lawmakers also face urgent decisions on government funding, defense legislation and leadership changes.

Source: Associated Press, November 9.

🇺🇦 2. UKRAINE — NEW PEACE TALKS OFFER UNCERTAIN HOPE

Russia and Ukraine are scheduled to resume American-mediated negotiations November 10–11 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, following months without direct negotiations involving U.S. mediators.

Security guarantees, disputed territory and the possibility of a ceasefire dominate discussions.
Russia seeks Ukrainian territorial concessions and limits on its military alliances. Ukraine demands protection against future invasion and opposes surrendering additional territory.

European leaders insist their security interests must be represented.

Fighting continues. No peace agreement has been reached.

Sources: Associated Press; Axios.

🇮🇷 3. MIDDLE EAST — IRAN WAR ENTERS CRITICAL DIPLOMATIC PHASE

Following approximately eight months of conflict, President Trump declared November 9 that the war against Iran was militarily "effectively over."

However, American forces remain deployed, naval restrictions continue, and a lasting settlement remains elusive.
Qatar is helping mediate negotiations concerning Iran's nuclear activities, sanctions and regional security.

Iran demands relief from economic restrictions and an end to hostilities. Washington insists on safeguards preventing nuclear weapons development.

Disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz have affected global energy supplies. A diplomatic breakthrough remains possible but unconfirmed.

Sources: Associated Press; Reuters.

🌍 4. EUROPE — G7 LEADERS CONFRONT GLOBAL DIVISIONS

Foreign ministers representing the United States, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan gathered in Paris November 9.

Their agenda includes Ukraine, Iran, international justice, energy security and artificial intelligence.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said America's foreign policy would remain under Trump's direction despite Republican election losses.

European governments are pressing for greater participation in peace negotiations. Significant disagreements remain over international courts and technology regulation.

Source: Associated Press.

🌡️ 5. CLIMATE — GLOBAL SUMMIT OPENS IN TURKEY

Representatives from nearly 200 countries are gathering in Antalya for COP31, running November 9–20.

United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell warned that existing progress remains inadequate.
Negotiators are considering expanded electrification, cleaner energy systems, adaptation funding and assistance for vulnerable nations.

Turkey proposes increasing electricity's share of worldwide energy consumption to approximately 35% by 2035.

The challenge is balancing economic development, energy security and emissions reductions while extreme weather intensifies.

Sources: Reuters; United Nations climate reporting.

💰 6. WORLD ECONOMY — OIL PRICES FALL AS DIPLOMACY ADVANCES

Oil prices declined sharply following signals that Washington might avoid renewed major military strikes against Iran.

Benchmark Brent crude settled near $92.57 per barrel November 9, although prices continued fluctuating afterward.
Markets are assessing economic growth, inflation, interest rates and possible changes in global petroleum supplies.

Lower oil prices could eventually ease transportation and production costs, but households may not experience immediate relief.

Source: Reuters.

🤖 7. TECHNOLOGY — NVIDIA FACES SECURITY SCRUTINY

Artificial intelligence leader Nvidia announced an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang following reports concerning an alleged relationship with a woman suspected of Chinese intelligence connections.

A shareholder lawsuit alleges inadequate disclosure of potential risks. Those allegations remain unproven.
Nvidia shares declined approximately 4.3% November 9.

The controversy highlights growing concerns surrounding corporate security, international espionage allegations and the enormous economic influence of AI technology.

Source: Reuters.

✝️ 8. FAITH AND HUMAN DIGNITY — POPE VISITS ARGENTINA

Pope Leo XIV continued his South American journey with a visit to Argentina, following Uruguay.

In meetings with Argentine leaders, including President Javier Milei, the pontiff emphasized human dignity and concern for vulnerable populations.
He also met survivors of clergy sexual abuse, bringing renewed attention to accountability within the Catholic Church.

The visit illustrates the continuing influence of religious leadership on discussions of poverty, justice and human responsibility.

Sources: Associated Press; Reuters.

🕊️ THE WORLD AT A CROSSROADS

November 9 reveals a world navigating political upheaval, uncertain peace negotiations, economic pressures, technological risks and environmental challenges.

The coming days could determine whether diplomacy brings meaningful progress in Ukraine and Iran, whether American political divisions deepen, and whether governments turn climate commitments into action.
THE CENTRAL QUESTION IS NOT SIMPLY WHAT WORLD LEADERS WILL PROMISE, BUT WHAT THEY WILL ACTUALLY DELIVER.

Behind every headline are families, communities and human lives affected by decisions made far beyond their borders.

Heaven's Pulse | World News Today

🇮🇷⚔️🇺🇸 Iran Reverse-Engineers Captured US Weapons as $9bn Nuclear Deal Emerges

TEHRAN, November 9, 2026 — Iran says its defence scientists have begun reverse-engineering American military equipment captured during the conflict with the United States, even as reports suggest Washington could release up to $9 billion in frozen Iranian funds under a proposed nuclear agreement.

Brigadier General Ali Balali, an adviser to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Aerospace Force, said Iranian specialists were examining seized American technology to strengthen the country's domestic weapons industry.

“Various pieces of equipment and a range of assets have been captured from the enemy,” Balali said, adding that engineers were working to extract technical knowledge from the material.

He did not identify the systems involved or provide independent evidence of the latest captures. However, Iran seized an American Dive-LD underwater drone near the Strait of Hormuz in September. US officials downplayed its intelligence value, while analysts said it could still offer insights into American autonomous systems.

Balali also claimed Iran had increased missile and drone production and built sufficient stockpiles to withstand renewed hostilities.

Meanwhile, Saudi broadcaster Al Arabiya cited unnamed sources suggesting that mediation by Qatar and Pakistan had revived negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

Under the reported framework, the United States could release between $6 billion and $9 billion in Iranian assets and accept uranium enrichment on Iranian soil up to 3.67%, a limit corresponding to the 2015 nuclear accord.

Discussions reportedly include renewed International Atomic Energy Agency inspections and arrangements to reduce Iran's stockpile of more highly enriched uranium.

In return, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington would lift its naval blockade, potentially easing pressure on international oil shipments.

However, no final agreement has been announced. Neither government has publicly confirmed the reported enrichment concessions, and Reuters reported on Monday that US and Gulf officials remained doubtful that a deal was imminent.

President Donald Trump has indicated he will avoid fresh large-scale strikes for now, although US forces remain deployed and the blockade continues.

Brady Press Briefing Room.On November 7, Trump publicly offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House Press Secretary position in a Truth Social post, even suggesting that several UFC fighters join him as assistants. White was in London for a Zuffa Boxing event when he reacted to the announcement, saying he was heading to Washington for a meeting with Trump.The following day, Trump clarified that the offer was a joke. But on November 9, White appeared alongside the president at the White House and stepped behind the briefing room podium.“I’ve always wanted to do this. Who has the first question?” White told reporters before making one thing clear: “I have zero political aspirations.”Trump continued joking about the position, while White thanked him and declined the job. The appearance brought together the worlds of UFC, politics and the White House in an unusual moment.

text:
One hurdle down. The Senate voted 73 to 25 on Monday to begin debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, the permitting overhaul written by Republicans Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee and Democrats Martin Heinrich and Sheldon Whitehouse. The AP called it the first major action in Congress since last week’s elections. President Trump has endorsed the bill, according to CNBC.

The 417 page bill would change the National Environmental Policy Act, the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act and the National Historic Preservation Act to speed up reviews for power plants, pipelines, mines and other projects, and it overhauls how new transmission lines get approved, CNBC reported. It would also make data center developers pay their own way for power and grid upgrades. “We cannot allow the costs of permitting delays to fall to the American people, as they have in the past,” Capito said, according to The Washington Times. She cited a White House Council of Economic Advisers estimate of $186 billion in economic output.

Monday’s vote only opened debate. Senators plan to offer amendments, and the bill still has to clear a second 60 vote hurdle before final passage, The Washington Times reported. Democrats are split. Sen. Ed Markey says he wants a better deal, and Earthjustice, the Sierra Club and the ACLU urged Democratic leaders to slow down, according to The Guardian. If it passes the Senate this week, it still needs the House before this Congress ends in January.

Seventy three votes in this Senate is no small thing. Making data centers pay for their own power instead of sticking families with the bill is just common sense. Finish it this week and send it to the House. Think the House gets it done before January?

Sources: AP, CNBC, The Washington Times, The Guardian, Law360

text:
An Open Letter to @potus @realDonaldTrump 

Mr. President: The Mandate Is Slipping Away

I write with respect for the office you hold and for the millions of Americans who trusted you with it. That trust is exactly why I cannot stay silent. On November 3rd, voters handed Congress to the Democrats. They did not ask for open borders again, and they did not suddenly embrace the left. They rendered a verdict on execution. A winning agenda has been badly carried out, and with two years left, the window to correct it is closing.

You won the border. Illegal crossings fell from nearly 250,000 a month in late 2023 to about 11,000 this August. No president in a generation achieved that, and you deserve full credit for it. But that victory has been overshadowed by masked agents, neighborhood raids, and at least nine people killed in shootings involving immigration agents. A Fox News poll found 53 percent of voters believe the crackdown has gone too far. In the Rio Grande Valley, Hispanic voters who came to you in 2024 turned away. These are not media inventions. They are the consequences of decisions made under your authority.

On immigration, strength and cruelty are not the same thing. Remove every violent criminal, and do it swiftly. The country stands with you on that. But pursuing landscapers, caregivers and cooks who have lived here peacefully for a decade does not make America safer. It wounds communities, divides the country, and costs you the moral authority the border victory earned. Offer those with clean records an earned legal status: fines, back taxes, background checks, and no place ahead of those who waited. Mandate E-Verify so this never happens again. You are the one president with the credibility to pass it. History will ask why you did not.

On life, absolutism is costing the movement the country. You have said you support exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother. Please say it again, clearly, and stand behind it. Every family raising a daughter has read accounts of women left waiting for care in medical emergencies. Draw a firm line at late-term abortion and take a national ban off the table. That is where most Americans stand, and it is where you have stood.

On Iran, America must finish what it started. This war began on February 28. Nine months later it remains a stalemate of strikes, talks, threats and more talks. Gas has hovered near $4 a gallon. The regime in Tehran is betting that our resolve will fade before its own does. Every deadline that passes without consequence confirms that bet.  God saved your life to help finish this evil regime.  Just do it or let Israel finish the job.

I say this next part with respect for the office of the Vice President, but plainly: JD Vance should not be leading this effort. He said in 2024 that war with Iran was not in America's interest. You have acknowledged that the two of you differ "philosophically" on it. In September, with strikes still flaring, he told the country he "wouldn't call it a war." He has not distanced himself from Tucker Carlson, who has called for your impeachment. The IRGC reads all of this. A negotiation led by someone who never believed in the cause signals the very hesitation our adversaries are counting on. Place this in the hands of those whose resolve is beyond question, define the end clearly, and achieve it: no enrichment, no path to a bomb, the Revolutionary Guard dismantled, and the Strait of Hormuz open.

On energy, the price at the pump is the true measure. America produces more oil than any nation in history, yet families are paying more than when you took office. Production numbers do not reach the kitchen table on their own. Hold producers and middlemen accountable, and make American energy lower American prices. Until it does, energy dominance remains a promise rather than a result.

On leadership, your words carry the weight of the presidency. Calling the press "treasonous scum" and feuding with the Pope do not project strength. They distract from your achievements and push away Americans you need. You have proven you can fight. The country now needs you to lead all of it, including those who did not vote for you. Firmness and dignity are not opposites. The most powerful voice in the world does not need to raise itself to be heard.

Dear @POTUS, you were sent to Washington to restore the country, and on the border you showed it can be done. The same courage is now required to correct course. You have two years to win back the trust of those who put you there. I hope, for the country's sake, that you will.

Respectfully.

text:
🇺🇸 A Republic, If You Can Keep It: The American Experiment at 250

America was never meant to be just another country.

The Founders called it an experiment. 📜

Not a kingdom. Not an inheritance. A test of whether ordinary people could govern themselves without kings, rulers, or power handed down by birth.

Washington said the fate of liberty was "staked on the experiment entrusted to the hands of the American people."

And it was never supposed to be an elitist country.

The promise was a fair and equal shot for everyone, regardless of race, religion, education, or economic background. The country did not live up to that promise at the start, and generations fought to widen it. But that promise is the whole point of the experiment. No ruling class. No one born ahead of the line.

That is also what makes free enterprise work. Anyone with an idea, a skill, and the will to work can compete, build, and win. 💡

But they understood something else too.

The greatest threat to freedom isn't always force. It's human nature. Comfort. Convenience. The slow, quiet habit of handing over responsibility because someone else offers to carry it.

When Franklin was asked what kind of government the convention had created, his answer came with a condition:

"A republic, if you can keep it."

If.

So look at where we stand in 2026, the year America turned 250. 📊

A Gallup survey this year found that fewer than half of Americans believe everyone in this country has the opportunity to achieve the American Dream.

At the same time, Federal Reserve data shows the top 1% of households hold 32.5% of the nation's wealth, the highest share since tracking began in 1989.

Let me be clear. Success is not the problem. Building wealth is not the problem. Free markets and free enterprise are how this country created more opportunity than any nation in history.

The question is whether the ladder is still there for the next person. 🪜 Whether someone starting with nothing today can still climb as high as their talent and work ethic will take them.

A free market depends on open competition and a fair shot. An elite class that pulls the ladder up behind it is the opposite of both.

Experiments don't run themselves. They need people who pay attention, ask hard questions, and refuse to trade freedom for ease.

250 years later, the question is still open:

Are we protecting the experiment, or slowly giving it away? 👇

#America250 #AmericanDream #Leadership #Opportunity #FreeEnterprise

China said Monday it was in communication with relevant parties about a possible meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia, following remarks by US President Donald Trump that they could meet next week to discuss ending the Iran war.

“China maintains communication with the relevant parties on the meeting between the three presidents,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular press briefing.

Asked about the proposed meeting in Shenzhen and its agenda, Guo added: “As for your specific question, I have no information to offer at the moment.”

Separately, asked about a Washington Post report that the Trump administration had sought China's help in ending the conflict with Iran, Guo called for a diplomatic resolution without confirming the reported request.

“To prolong the conflict between the U.S. and Iran does not serve the common interest of the parties concerned and the international community,” he said.

Guo urged the parties to resolve their differences through dialogue and negotiations and restore peace in the Middle East and Persian Gulf region.

Orange County California - Coastal Risk Analysis and Forecast

NEW HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR LOS ANGELES COUNTY BEACHES; WEST-FACING COASTS FACE GREATER WAVE IMPACTS.

Forecast issued: November 9, 2026 — Afternoon update
Current risk: MODERATE RISK across Orange County; locally HIGH RISK on exposed Los Angeles County beaches.
Scale: LOW → MODERATE → HIGH → SEVERE

WHAT MATTERS NOW

The National Weather Service expanded its High Surf Advisory to Los Angeles County beaches at 1:34 PM PST. Breaking waves of 5–8 feet are expected on exposed west-facing beaches through noon Tuesday, alongside the existing Coastal Flood Advisory.

This is a significant location-specific hazard increase. The larger westerly swell creates greater wave-run-up and erosion concerns along exposed beaches, while south-facing shorelines receive less direct wave energy. 

Los Angeles County beaches — Locally HIGH RISK. West-facing beaches face 5–8-foot breakers, dangerous rip currents and increased erosion. Flooding remains possible around high tide.

Newport/Balboa and Huntington/Sunset — MODERATE RISK, locally HIGH RISK possible. October flooding involved elevated water and southerly swell. For this event, westerly wave exposure differs, but elevated water and run-up remain concerns. Berm protection is not assured.

Laguna Beach — MODERATE RISK. October flooding demonstrated vulnerability to high water and wave run-up. Exposed west-facing sections warrant continued attention.

Dana Point/Capistrano Beach — MODERATE RISK. September 7 produced damaging overtopping, particularly in Capistrano Beach. Today’s swell direction offers some shelter, but narrow beaches and exposed revetments remain vulnerable.

San Clemente — MODERATE RISK, locally HIGH RISK possible. West-facing beaches face increased wave run-up and dangerous swimming conditions.

Long Beach — MODERATE RISK. NWS specifically identifies reduced exposure to this westerly swell compared with previous southerly-swell events. Elevated harbor water and drainage flooding remain separate concerns.

MEASURED OCEAN CONDITIONS

Water level: NWS continues forecasting Tuesday morning’s peak ocean level above 7 feet, approximately 14–17 inches above astronomical predictions. This is a forecast, not an independently verified gauge residual.

Buoy observations: The available November 9 readings show substantial offshore-to-nearshore differences:

• Capistrano Beach: 3.08 ft / 15.4 sec / SW 221°.
• Oceanside offshore: 3.22 ft / 16.7 sec / SW 235°.
• San Pedro: 3.05 ft / 15.4 sec / W 271°.
• Santa Monica Bay: 4.20 ft / 14.3 sec / W 264°.

These observations are from earlier today and do not establish current evening conditions or trends.

Observation versus forecast: Nearshore wave heights remain substantially below the largest forecast breaking waves at exposed locations. Significant buoy wave height and breaking surf are different measurements. 

5-DAY COASTAL RISK FORECAST

Tuesday — MODERATE to locally HIGH RISK: Morning high water, dangerous west-facing surf; advisories through noon.

Wednesday — MODERATE RISK, potentially easing: Verify declining wave energy and water levels.

Thursday — LOW to MODERATE RISK: Reassess shoreline conditions after the swell.

Friday — LOW to MODERATE RISK: Coastal hazards depend on developing weather conditions.

Saturday — Forecast confidence limited: Updated marine forecasts needed.

Beyond day five: November 24–26 king tides remain a separate coastal-risk window.

SOURCES: NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard Coastal Hazard Message, November 9, 1:34 PM PST; NWS San Diego Coastal Flood Advisory, 2:58 PM PST; CDIP buoy observations.

"You want to deport illegal aliens, but I don't see YOU picking vegetables, cleaning hotel rooms, or doing roofing work!"

Do you understand WHY Americans aren't lining up for these jobs?  It's because employers have access to a large pool of cheap labor from people who have very little bargaining power.

This is basic economics.  When employers can fill positions at low wages, there's less pressure to raise those wages or improve working conditions.

Before someone starts screaming about capitalism, let me explain something.  Capitalism depends on competition. That includes employers competing for WORKERS.

If you can't find someone willing to pick vegetables for $10 an hour, perhaps you need to offer $15. Or $20. Or invest in automation.  Or improve working conditions.

That's how a labor market is SUPPOSED to work.

I have similar objections to the H-1B visa system.  When a worker's immigration status depends heavily on an employer, that employer has leverage that an ordinary American worker doesn't have to tolerate.

And that brings me to something else.

Would removing illegal labor cause prices to rise in some industries?  Probably. Would every displaced job automatically go to an American? Of course not. working conditions when doing so might jeopardize their livelihoods or expose them to immigration enforcement.

That doesn't just hurt them. It can undermine bargaining power across the labor market.

Would removing illegal labor cause prices to rise in some industries? Probably. Would every displaced job automatically go to an American? Of course not.

But employers would have to adapt to a labor market in which they couldn't rely so heavily on workers with limited bargaining power.

If your business model depends on a permanent supply of cheap, vulnerable labor, perhaps the problem isn't that Americans refuse to work.

Perhaps the problem is your business model.

💠 BALI PRATIPADA, celebrated on the first day of the bright fortnight of the Hindu month of Kartik (Kartik Shukla Pratipada), marks the triumphant yet benevolent return of the Asura King Mahabali to Earth and celebrates the virtue of absolute surrender (Atmanivedanq) to Lord Sri Vishnu's Vamana avatar. Falling as the fourth day of the Diwali festivities, it is recognized in sacred texts like the Dharmasindhu as one of the three-and-a-half most spiritually potent and auspicious Muhurtas (timings) of the entire year.

✨ Details of the Festival:-
According to Puranic history, King Mahabali was a highly righteous and charitable demon king whose immense power threatened the cosmic balance. Lord Sri Vishnu incarnated as the dwarf Brahmin, Vamana, and asked for three paces of land. When Bali agreed, Sri Vamana expanded into His cosmic Trivikrama form, covering the earthly realm in His first step and the heavenly skies in His second. With no land left, Mahabali humbly offered his own head for the third step, fully surrendering his ego. Pleased by his absolute devotion, Sri Vishnu granted him a boon allowing him to step out of Patala Loka (the underworld) to visit his subjects on Earth once every year.

✨ Regional names and practices vary widely across the subcontinent:

Maharashtra - Bali Padwa
Wives apply tilak to husbands, exchange gifts, and draw five-colored rangolis.

Gujarat & Rajasthan - Bestu Varas
Celebrated as the traditional New Year Day marking the start of the Vikram Samvat.

Karnataka & Andhra - Bali Padyami
Families build structures in cattle sheds, worship cows, and play a ritualistic dice game called Pachikalu.

Tulunadu (Coastal KA) - Balinda Lepuna
At midnight, families plant a decorated branch in fields/sheds and shout "Coup!" to call the King home.

✨ The Esoteric Secrets of Bali Pratipada:-
Beyond the basic story of charity and standard Diwali greetings, ancient texts and Tantric traditions hold deeper, hidden meanings regarding this specific day:

The Secret of the Future Indra: A hidden detail in the Matsya and Brahma Puranas is that Mahabali’s banishment to Patala was not a punishment, but a divine protection and promotion. Lord Sri Vishnu granted Mahabali the boon that he will become the Indra (King of Heaven) during the next Manvantara (cosmic age) called Savarni Manvantara. His current stay in the underworld is considered a period of spiritual preparation under the personal guardianship of Lord Sri Vishnu.

The Dyuta Pratipada (Sacred Gambling): In scripture, this day is also called Dyutapratipada. A major ritual rule prescribes playing games of chance or dice (Pachikalu) on this morning. Esoterically, the dice game represents the unpredictable wheel of cosmic time (Kala). It is believed that Lord Shiv and Mother Parvati played dice on this day; winning or actively engaging in it cheerfully sets a psychological tone of resilience, joy, and abundance for the coming year.

The Illusion of Loss: The deeper Vedantic secret of Bali Pratipada lies in the paradox of Bali's defeat. By losing his earthly kingdom, Mahabali gained Lord Sri Vishnu Himself, Who promised to stand eternally as the gatekeeper of Bali's palace in the underworld. The day teaches the secret of Atmanivedan—that when a seeker surrenders their individual ego (symbolized by Bali's head) to the Divine, they do not actually lose anything; rather, the Divine becomes bound to them.

The Margapali Ritual: An ancient practice mentioned in the Dharmasindhu involves tying a Margapali (a protective rope woven from Kusha grass) across the village roads between a pole and a tree. The entire community, along with their decorated cattle, passes underneath it. This ritual acts as a spiritual filter to cleanse the community of negative energies, plagues, and evil omens carried over from the dark half of the year.

Claiming the maintenance job was a secret cover for CCT duties is an insult to every actual Special Tactics airman who earned the scarlet beret by surviving the pipeline, and it is an insult to the maintenance people at Pope who did their job without pretending they were something else. I was there. The 41st was not running a classified CCT cover program out of the dual-rail shop. It was an airlift squadron. The records match the unit. Barber’s story does not. @PopeField @41AS and every airman who actually served there know the difference.

NewsNation and Ross Coulthart packaged this as an elite résumé: recruited into Combat Control, helicopter pilot, freefall parachutist, expert marksman, NATO top-secret clearance, Bosnia heroism. That is what they sold. Barber himself changed the story in longer interviews into the “gateway then cover” version. Both versions are fake. The NATO clearance references are routine travel paperwork for anyone who deploys on a NATO mission. They are not a special top-secret SOF clearance. The heroism claims and advanced qualifications do not appear as CCT-level achievements on the documents that were shown. The three former special operations personnel cited as corroboration offered personal statements. Personal statements do not override the official service record on AFSC, training completion, and unit assignment. When the paperwork and the unit say one thing and the story says another, the paperwork wins.

This is what stolen valor looks like. It is not only the guy who buys a beret and pins on badges he never earned. It is the guy who takes the reputation, the training, the risk, and the brotherhood of the people who actually finished the pipeline and grafts it onto his own civilian narrative so that media outlets, podcasts, and eventually a congressional office will treat him as a tier-one operator. Combat Controllers are FAA-certified air traffic controllers who can jump, dive, shoot, and control airstrikes in the worst environments on earth. They earn that by surviving selection and nearly two years of continuous training that most people quit or fail. They are not airplane mechanics who washed out of the pipeline, served at an airlift squadron, and later decided the mechanic job made a better cover story for UFO content. When @jakebarber2025 and the people who amplified him sell the CCT framing, they are stepping on every actual CCT, PJ, and Special Tactics airman who paid the real price for those qualifications. That is disrespect. It is theft of the one thing those men and women earned that cannot be faked: the record of having finished what almost everyone else did not.

The civilian helicopter work after separation is documented in ordinary federal contracting records for firefighting and related aviation support through companies associated with him (San Joaquin Helicopters, Coastal Helicopters, Royal Helicopter Services). It does not erase the fact that the special-operations credentials that made the story marketable do not match the service record. Post-service contractor work is not a retroactive promotion to Combat Controller. 

SkyWatcher and the related psionic/summoning crap he helped launch do not change the military record either.
Now he is on the staff of Representative Eric Burlison, working UAP issues after David Grusch ran off. 

@RepEricBurlison, your office hired a man whose public military narrative has been contradicted by his own DD-214, by the unit he was actually assigned to at Pope, by the training timeline, and by every veteran who has looked at the paperwork without a financial or narrative incentive to believe the cover story. You are employing a washed-out maintenance airman as if the difference between an E-4 aerospace maintenance journeyman and a Combat Controller is a minor detail that can be papered over with a “cover job” explanation.

How personalized vaccines are changing the fight against brain cancer
UCLA researchers are advancing cancer vaccines that train the immune system to recognize and attack brain tumors, offering new possibilities for patients diagnosed with one of the deadliest forms of cancer📷Dr. Linda Liau examines clinical trial patient Jamil Newirth. (Photo by Milo Mitchell)November 9, 2026By Denise Heady, MA7 min readWhen Jamil Newirth was just 32 years old, doctors told him he had terminal brain cancer and had about 17 months to live.That was 14 years https://t.co/8JzXPOmybR, at 46, the Hawaii native is a practicing attorney in Maui, a future he once feared he would never have. He credits his remarkable survival in part to a novel cancer vaccine developed at UCLA that uses the body's own immune system to recognize and attack brain tumors.Newirth is among a group of patients who have experienced long-term survival after receiving the personalized vaccine through clinical trials led by UCLA neurosurgeon Linda Liau, MD, PhD and tumor immunologist Robert Prins, PhD.For more than two decades, Dr. Liau and her team at the UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center have been working to develop new treatments for glioblastoma, the most aggressive and deadly form of brain cancer. Their work is now helping shape the next generation of cancer vaccines and combination immunotherapies that could offer new hope for patients facing this devastating disease."Patients like Jamil are such an inspiration to me and my team," said Dr. Liau, chair of neurosurgery at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA. "He and other patients like him are what inspires me to go to work each day and to maintain hope that immunotherapy could potentially lead to a cure for brain cancer someday."A devastating diagnosis
In 2012, Newirth had just graduated from the University of Hawaii William S. Richardson School of Law and was preparing for the bar exam when he began experiencing severe headaches.After multiple emergency room visits, where his symptoms were initially attributed to stress, he developed nausea, vomiting and numbness on the left side of his body. An MRI eventually revealed a large brain tumor. He was diagnosed with glioblastoma.Glioblastoma grows and spreads quickly.  Even after standard treatments such as surgery, chemotherapy and radiation, the disease almost always returns."I wasn't really given any hope when I was diagnosed," Newirth recalled.📷Jamil Newirth found Dr. Linda Liau when he was searching for neurosurgeons investigating new treatments for glioblastoma. (Photo by Milo Mitchell)Determined to find another option, he began searching for a neurosurgeon who could offer something beyond standard treatment. That search led him to Dr. Liau, who was enrolling patients in a clinical trial testing the first personalized brain cancer vaccine."Dr. Liau is confident, caring and does everything with a personal touch," Newirth said. "She even flew back early from her vacation to do my surgery and start my treatment. You can tell she just really cares."Teaching the immune system to fight brain cancer
One of the biggest challenges in treating glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors is that the tumors are particularly effective at evading the immune system. Unlike some other cancers, these tumors often contain relatively few of the immune cells (also known as killer T cells) needed to recognize and attack cancer.Dr. Liau and Dr. Prins have spent years investigating whether a personalized vaccine could help overcome that barrier.The vaccine, an autologous tumor lysate-pulsed dendritic cell vaccination (ATL-DC) known as DCVax-L, was developed to help overcome this challenge by teaching the body to recognize proteins found in a patient's https://t.co/aenOhGWFPW create the vaccine, initially developed at UCLA, researchers collect tumor tissue removed during surgery and isolate immune cells called dendritic cells generated from the patient's own blood. These cells act as messengers for the immune system, helping it identify https://t.co/JcWR50KI81 the laboratory, the dendritic cells are exposed to proteins from the patient's tumor, essentially training them to recognize and attack the cancer. When the cells are injected back into the patient, they help activate an immune response directed against the tumor.Unlike traditional vaccines, which are typically given to prevent disease, this therapeutic vaccine is designed to help the immune system fight an existing cancer.The approach is especially promising because each vaccine is tailored to the individual patient's tumor.“This is a personalized vaccine that we developed and have spearheaded all the way from the initial preclinical studies to the original first-in-human clinical trial, to newer work testing novel formulations of the vaccine combined with adjuvants and immune checkpoint blockade,” said Dr. Prins.For Newirth, the experimental treatment offered a possibility that conventional therapies alone could not guarantee.While undergoing treatment, Newirth continued studying for the bar exam and ultimately passed. He credits the innovative research from Dr. Liau and her team for saving his life.And he is not https://t.co/8XhkYCsfXk far, approximately two dozen patients who received the vaccine through clinical trials have become long-term survivors. Their experiences are particularly meaningful for a disease where survival beyond five years remains uncommon.However, the vaccine does not benefit everyone, and researchers are still working to understand why some patients respond more favorably than others.“There is a significant subgroup of patients who have lived more than five years,” Dr. Liau says. “But the challenge is trying to determine which patients it may work for and for which patients it doesn’t. Each new discovery gets us closer to improving survival and quality of life for patients facing this devastating disease.”Building on the promise of cancer vaccines
The encouraging responses seen in some patients have helped shape the next phase of Dr. Liau's research.Rather than relying on the vaccine alone, her team is now investigating whether combining it with other immunotherapies could produce stronger and more lasting https://t.co/DOle5MtiPU approach involves pairing the vaccine with immune checkpoint inhibitors, a class of drugs that helps immune cells overcome signals that prevent them from attacking cancer.Although checkpoint inhibitors have transformed treatment for several cancers, they have shown limited success against glioblastoma when used alone. One reason may be that brain tumors often lack sufficient numbers of cancer-fighting T cells for these drugs to activate.The vaccine could help address that problem by first teaching the immune system to recognize the tumor and drawing cancer-fighting T cells into it. Checkpoint inhibitors could then enhance the function of those T cells within the tumor and help them remain active.Dr. Liau’s team is also investigating which treatments work best together, and the order in which they should be given. Researchers hope that understanding how to sequence these treatments could make them more effective against tumors that have historically resisted immunotherapy.“Because of the heterogeneity of glioblastoma, I don’t think there is going to be one drug or one treatment that is going to be effective for all patients. The future of glioblastoma treatments is going to be these combination approaches,” said Dr. Liau.Scientists are also exploring other types of cancer vaccines, including vaccines designed to target specific genetic mutations found in brain tumors.Some newer vaccines are designed to target molecular features shared by patients with the same type of cancer. This approach could help researchers develop treatments for specific groups of patients without needing to identify unique targets from each person's tumor.Building on this research, UCLA neurosurgeon Anthony Wang, MD, director of the Pediatric Brain Tumor Program at UCLA Health, is leading a clinical trial testing a new vaccine for a rare and aggressive type of brain cancer called H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma, which primarily affects adolescents and young adults. The vaccine targets abnormal proteins produced by changes in how tumor cells process genetic information, with the goal of helping the immune system recognize and attack the cancer.Developed in collaboration with Dr. Liau and Dr. Prins, the vaccine uses patients' own dendritic cells to activate an immune response against these tumor-specific targets. The first-in-human trial is designed to evaluate the vaccine's safety and explore whether it can generate a lasting immune response against the cancer.More time, more possibilities
For Dr. Liau, the long-term survivors who have emerged from these clinical trials offer an important reason to keep pushing forward. Each patient provides valuable insight into how the immune system responds to brain cancer and how future treatments might be improved.Her goal is to build on those discoveries so that more patients can benefit from treatments that once seemed out of reach.For Newirth, the opportunity to participate in a clinical trial changed the course of his life. Fourteen years after being told he had little time left, he has built a life and career that once seemed impossible.“The hope is that stories like Newirth's will one day become less of an exception and more of a reality for patients facing brain cancer,” said Dr. Liau.

text:
No publicly announced data center (or other major development) is planned specifically for Marshall County’s Opportunity Zone Tract 301.
Tract 301 (roughly 52,000 acres, shown in the ADECA map in the image) is an original 2018 Opportunity Zone (OZ 1.0). These zones remain in effect through the end of 2028 and offer federal tax incentives for private investment in lower-income census tracts. They do not authorize, require, or propose any particular project.
Buck’s Pocket State Park and Lake Guntersville State Park are public lands managed by Alabama State Parks and are not open to private commercial development in the way private or other lands might be. The large census tract includes private land (forests, farmland, etc.) outside the parks, which could theoretically attract investment, but no specific commercial projects targeting the area have been announced in news reports, economic development filings, or public records tied to this tract.
Broader context
Alabama has seen a surge in data center proposals and construction (Meta, Google, and others in places like Huntsville, Jackson County, Bessemer, Lowndes, and elsewhere), driven by AI demand, power availability, land, and incentives. Rural Opportunity Zones are especially attractive for large capital-intensive projects like hyperscale data centers because of the tax benefits (and enhanced rural rules under OZ 2.0 starting in 2027). However, the newly designated OZ 2.0 tracts in Marshall County are 308.04 and 311—not Tract 301.
The social media post raises a valid transparency concern about what might happen on private land in a big Opportunity Zone near sensitive natural areas. At this point, though, there is no evidence of a data center or other major project advancing there. Local officials, ADECA, or land records would be the places to monitor for any future proposals.

On November 10, 1903, Mary Anderson received a U.S. patent for a windshield wiper inspired by a snowy streetcar ride in New York City. Back home in Birmingham, Alabama, she designed a rubber blade the driver could sweep across the glass using a lever inside the vehicle. When Anderson later offered her patent to a Canadian firm, the company passed. It saw too little commercial value in a device that would eventually become standard on cars.

🚨 GOOGLE TELLS SCHOOLS: ACCEPT AI-POWERED SEARCH OR LOSE GOOGLE SEARCH ACCESS — FREDERICK SCHOOL BOARD PUSHES BACK

Frederick County school officials are confronting a new dilemma after Google announced that schools rejecting its AI features could also lose access to traditional Google Search.

The controversy comes just weeks after Frederick County’s Board of Education voted 6–1 on October 7 to prohibit student AI use, with exceptions for legally required accommodations.

▪️ GOOGLE’S POLICY: Schools can disable Gemini and other AI tools, but Google says AI is now integrated into Search, preventing districts from retaining a fully AI-free version.

▪️ FREDERICK’S POSITION: Board members have raised concerns about student safety, cheating, critical thinking and the district’s ability to control classroom technology.

▪️ PARENTAL CONCERNS: Families and educators across Maryland are questioning whether schools have become too dependent on a single technology company.

▪️ NATIONAL BACKLASH: Critics accuse Google of using its dominant position in school technology to pressure districts into accepting AI.

Google argues its approach improves learning and gives administrators more control over student access.

But the controversy raises a serious question about public education and corporate influence.

Should a technology company effectively determine whether schools can offer basic internet search without AI?

Frederick County taxpayers deserve to know whether their school system can reject unwanted features without losing essential educational tools.

text:
Glad we agree God changes hearts. And for what it's worth, I held your view for most of my life. I understood my own conversion as my decision. I came to this one slowly, from the text.

So the real question isn't whether God changes hearts. It's when. Does He give the new heart before someone first comes to Christ, or after?

If it's after, then the heart that chose Christ was still the old one. But Paul says "the carnal mind is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, nor indeed can be" (Rom 8:7). Jesus says no one can even see the kingdom without being born again (John 3:3). If it's before, then we agree on more than you think. Ezekiel puts it in that order: "I will give you a new heart... I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes" (Ezek 36:26-27).

On choices not being real, that's not what Calvinists teach. The Westminster Confession says that by God's decree "neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures; nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established" (WCF 3.1). Scripture shows both at once. Joseph's brothers really chose evil: "you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good" (Gen 50:20). The men who crucified Jesus used "lawless hands," and it happened "by the determined purpose and foreknowledge of God" (Acts 2:23). Real choices, real guilt, God still sovereign.

So if God allows the same choice to two people and one believes while the other doesn't, what made the difference? "Who makes you differ from another?" (1 Cor 4:7)

Lynne-Marie Ruckert didn’t hesitate when she was asked to describe one of her honored Home Instead® employees.

“Clara is a quiet hero,” said Lynne-Marie, a human resources representative for owner Lisa Rabito’s award-winning franchise in Metairie, Louisiana, that serves the Orleans and Jefferson Parishes. “Clara is one of our Care Professionals of the Month who shows up when she is scheduled, goes above and beyond the call of duty for her clients and displays Home Instead®’s guiding principles of ‘Build Trust, Take the Lead and Share Your Heart.’ ”

Clara, a humble senior-care superstar who joined the franchise in December 2021, shines brightly among Home Instead’s amazing team of Care Pros by letting her caregiving feats speak for her. “For three days a week,” Lynne-Marie explained, “Clara cares for a gentleman who suffers from Alzheimer’s disease. She has been one of his primary Care Pros since July 2024.”

Lynne-Marie added: “Clara is very patient with her client. Using her gift of discernment that blends perfectly with her experience, Clara has learned when to motivate her client to stay active – which is very important to his health – and when to give him a break.”

In general, Clara takes time to learn about her clients and can use their clues, however subtle, to make sure they are happier when she leaves than when she arrived. When providing personal care for her client, sometimes he needs a moment to regroup. Clara will allow him the time and approach him differently or with some songs or old stories. That allows Clara to provide the needed care.

To build on their knowledge and experience, Clara and her fellow Care Pros in Metairie are offered the opportunity to increase their dementia-care skills by taking part in the Home Instead network’s one-of-a-kind training protocol. Home Instead’s Person-Centered Care Training for Alzheimer’s Disease and Other Dementias is recognized by the Alzheimer’s Association® for incorporating the evidence-based dementia-care practice recommendations in these topic areas: Alzheimer’s and dementia, person-centered care, assessment and care planning, activities of daily living, and behaviors and communication.

Clara provides the best possible care without the expectation of being recognized for it. Lynne-Marie said: “When I presented Clara with her Care Pro of the Month award, she was shocked and happy. Her smile said it all. She was honored and was going to share her award with her client’s daughter! We talked about families, and she joked that she is sometimes calmer at her client’s home, even on a challenging day, than dealing with her son and his ‘terrible 2s.’ ”

Clara is an important part of the Care Pro team at the New Orleans-area franchise, a member of a network comprised of Home Instead, Inc. and its parent company, Honor. With the world’s largest home-care network and the most advanced care platform, Honor and Home Instead are revolutionizing care for older adults, their families and Care Pros. Combined, the network has more than 100,000 Care Pros who are meeting the growing needs of millions of older adults and their families worldwide.

text:
Both the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) and Vanderbilt University were claimed on November 9, 2026, by the BYOD ransomware group.
Details on the two
•Texas HHSC (the state agency handling Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, and other public assistance programs): BYOD claimed access to data tied to roughly 2 million Texas residents, describing it as larger than a prior smaller leak of about 94,000 records. The claim includes references to Medicaid, banking information, and other program data. This is a claim on the group’s leak site; independent confirmation of the full scope is not public yet.
•Vanderbilt University: The university confirmed an active cybersecurity incident affecting devices, systems, and cloud services, and instructed people to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. BYOD claimed it locked databases and obtained research data plus personal information (SSNs, names, emails, phones, student and employee records) on over 1 million people. Vanderbilt Health (the separate medical organization) stated its systems were not impacted and patient care continued.
Other organizations recently claimed by BYOD
BYOD is a relatively new ransomware/data-extortion group that appeared in fall 2026. Other notable claims include:
•Michigan State University — claimed personal data on ~1.3 million current and former students.
•University of New Mexico / UNM Health — claimed a large-scale compromise (tens of thousands of systems, student/employee PII, research data, and some hospital systems). The incident disrupted care (ambulance diversions and canceled appointments at the state’s Level 1 trauma center). The group later offered free decryption for the hospital side and up to $2,500 per affected patient while saying it would retain the data; UNM described a more limited impact on some end-user devices.
•IHG Hotels & Resorts — claimed guest, loyalty, and related data access via a weak credential.
•Earlier/smaller claims have included entities such as Trump Mobile, related telecom samples, Gate (crypto exchange), and various retail/manufacturing firms.
Ransomware groups often inflate or partially fabricate claims, so the listed data volumes and full system access should be treated as unverified until the organizations or independent forensics confirm them. Vanderbilt’s public statement acknowledges an incident but has not confirmed the full BYOD claims or data theft scale. Texas HHSC has not issued a matching public confirmation in the available reports.
If you’re asking because of personal data exposure risk (e.g., as a student, employee, or Texas benefits recipient), monitor official notices from the organizations and consider standard steps like credit monitoring if notified.

Do you really not understand why the original Big 12 split after 2009 and Texas’ role in it?

Nebraska learned of a plot where Texas, A&M, Tech, Colorado, OU and Oklahoma State were planning to join the PAC-10 to form the first 16-team super conference. Fearing stability issues and being left behind, they called the Big Ten.

The main reason realignment was even on the table was Texas wasn’t satisfied. The PAC-16 super conference nearly happened, but ESPN stepped in and offered Texas a pile of money for the Longhorn Network to keep them from leaving the Big 12. ESPN couldn’t lose Texas to what would have been a Fox aligned super conference.

Colorado ended up leaving for the PAC-12 anyways given how unstable the Big 12 had become with Texas being dissatisfied and then accepting the Longhorn Network deal at the expense of having a Big 12 network deal. A&M got super pissed about the LHN and left for the SEC. Missouri got left since the SEC had to take two schools.

All of this was a plan by ESPN to destroy the Big 12 and shove the biggest brands into the SEC, which ESPN has an interest in.

The Big 12 was a strong conference from 1996-2009. It appeared in as many national championship games as the SEC and many more than the Big Ten, ACC, and PAC-10.  The Big 12 was a threat to the SEC and Big Ten.  ESPN was working Texas for years to blow up the conference.

So the rub from me with Texas is we could have had so much more balance in college football had they exercised steady leadership to keep the original Big 12 together.

It’s like they joined the conference in 1996 but didn’t seem really committed? Or just biding their time? If so, that made them shitty partners then.

Trump said Huang told him he had no idea the woman was a spy.  Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation after reports surfaced Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence operation

The agency said that it's requiring GLP-1 drugs such as Eli Lilly's, Munjiro and Zebo, and Novo Nordisk's, Ozempic, and Wigovi to add information about the potential increased risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. The condition is a common cause of sudden painless vision loss and could lead to permanent impairment of sight in some cases, Bill Rakoff, Worldwide News Network. ”
